found: MEDIUM: a waiting hourly re-check dropped at midnight was never re-armed (the re-check alarm is one-shot), stranding its reports for about a day, and the same drop skipped a late-evening daily sync. FIXED: a wait is carried over midnight and started at the next free moment; check red first.

MEDIUM: two alarms firing in the same tick could start a run twice (Flipkart's twenty requests spent twice) or lose a wait. FIXED: every read-then-write of the stored wait goes through one chain (oneAtATime); check red first.
MEDIUM: an error in the daily start lost the waiting re-check. FIXED: each waiting start is tried on its own, a failure is warned about and the next still runs; check red first.

LOW: weak check 'leaves no ask-again alarm' made real (startWhenFree now clears the alarm when nothing else waits); the order daily-then-recheck pinned in background.test.js; panel wording made plainer and given a time reference.
LOW (both reviews): a damaged stored value (NaN, a name like __proto__) is dropped on read, in carryOnWaiting and whatIsWaiting.

NAMED, NOT FIXED (LOW): startWhenFree removes the wait before calling start, so a start that throws loses that run, as it did before this change. If the computer is in use all day the run does not start that day; the wait is carried to the next free moment and the panel says it is waiting.
NOT BUILT, asked of Control: what happens if he starts using the computer DURING a run. Today a run carries on; Click checks only at the start of a round. No pause was invented.
